title: A smooth ring map is standard smooth after inverting an element outside a given prime
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ a prime ideal. Then there is $g\in A$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $A_g$ of $A$ at $\{1,g,g^2,\dots\}$, viewed as an $R$-algebra via $R\to A\to A_g$, is standard smooth [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00TA (label lemma-smooth-syntomic, line 37438): Spec(A) is covered by standard opens D(g) with A_g standard smooth over R; the open D(g) of this covering that contains q gives the statement

mathlib_searches.query: smooth algebra is standard smooth after localizing at an element not in a given prime
If R → S is a smooth ring map and p is a prime of S, there is f not in p such that S_f is standard smooth over R
